preamble: Loss of glottalization in the glottalized labio-velar approximant [wˀ] (Americanist w̓). It is part of a wider loss of glottalized resonants on the Northwest Coast. In Makah the Proto-Southern-Wakashan glottalized sonorants merged with the plain ones, with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (Davidson 2002: 76, citing Jacobsen 1968): Nuu-chah-nulth cuw̓it, Makah cu·wit 'silver salmon'. Upriver Halkomelem lost resonant glottalization, usually lengthening the preceding vowel, while Island and Downriver keep it (Compton & Gerdts c. 2005). For the Chimakuan languages, the correspondence table in Wikipedia's Chimakuan languages article (after Powell 1974) gives the reflexes of the glottalized resonants as R or ʔR, *w̓ appearing in Quileute as w or ʔw. The Quileute words in the same article's numeral table, such as ƚáʔw 'two', show a glottal stop followed by a plain w, so the glottalization may survive as a separate segment rather than be lost; they are not listed as examples here. According to the same table, Chemakum instead hardened *w̓ to (ʔ)kʷ.
